title: CORS Middleware
description: Enable Cross-Origin Resource Sharing to allow frontend apps to communicate with your API.

slides.title: What is CORS? 🌐
slides.content:
# Cross-Origin Resource Sharing

Browsers enforce the **same-origin policy**: a web page can only make requests to the same domain. CORS allows a server to specify which origins are allowed to access its resources.

Without CORS, a frontend running on `localhost:3000` cannot call your API on `localhost:8000`.

**FastAPI** provides `CORSMiddleware` to handle this.

slides.title: Adding CORS Middleware
slides.content:
```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app = FastAPI()

origins = [
    "http://localhost:3000",
    "https://myfrontend.com",
]

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=origins,          # list of allowed origins
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],             # all HTTP methods
    allow_headers=["*"],             # all headers
)
```

quizData.question: What is the purpose of CORS middleware?

options.text: To allow web pages from other origins to access your API

quizData.explanation: CORS is a browser security mechanism that requires servers to explicitly allow cross-origin requests.
